title.hu: Folyamatos befejezett jelen (I have been working)
title.en: The Present Perfect Continuous (I have been working)
title.es: El presente perfecto continuo (I have been working)
title.de: Das Present Perfect Continuous (I have been working)

text.hu: A present perfect continuous szerkezete: have / has + been + ige-ing: „I have been waiting”, „she has been working”. Azt mondja, hogy egy cselekvés a múltban kezdődött, és még tart, vagy épp most fejeződött be, és látszik a nyoma. A spanyol „llevo + gerundio” megfelelője: „Llevo dos horas esperando” = „I have been waiting for two hours”.
text.en: The present perfect continuous is formed with have / has + been + verb-ing: “I have been waiting”, “she has been working”. It says that an action started in the past and is still going on, or has just stopped and you can see the result. It matches the Spanish “llevo + gerundio”: “Llevo dos horas esperando” = “I have been waiting for two hours”.
text.es: El presente perfecto continuo se forma con have / has + been + verbo-ing: «I have been waiting», «she has been working». Dice que una acción empezó en el pasado y todavía continúa, o acaba de parar y se ve el resultado. Equivale al «llevo + gerundio» del español: «Llevo dos horas esperando» = «I have been waiting for two hours».
text.de: Das Present Perfect Continuous wird mit have / has + been + Verb-ing gebildet: „I have been waiting“, „she has been working“. Es sagt, dass eine Handlung in der Vergangenheit begonnen hat und noch andauert oder gerade aufgehört hat und man das Ergebnis sieht. Es entspricht dem spanischen „llevo + gerundio“: „Llevo dos horas esperando“ = „I have been waiting for two hours“.

text.hu: Állító: have / has + been + ige-ing. Rövid alak: I’ve been, she’s been. Tagadás: haven’t / hasn’t + been + ige-ing.
text.en: Affirmative: have / has + been + verb-ing. Short form: I’ve been, she’s been. Negative: haven’t / hasn’t + been + verb-ing.
text.es: Afirmativa: have / has + been + verbo-ing. Forma corta: I’ve been, she’s been. Negación: haven’t / hasn’t + been + verbo-ing.
text.de: Bejahend: have / has + been + Verb-ing. Kurzform: I’ve been, she’s been. Verneinung: haven’t / hasn’t + been + Verb-ing.

examples.es: I have been waiting for an hour.

tr.en: I have been waiting for an hour.
tr.de: Ich warte schon seit einer Stunde.

text.hu: Kérdés: Have / Has + alany + been + ige-ing. How long…? kérdéssel az időtartamot kérdezzük. Rövid válasz: Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.
text.en: Question: Have / Has + subject + been + verb-ing. With How long…? we ask about the duration. Short answers: Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.
text.es: Pregunta: Have / Has + sujeto + been + verbo-ing. Con How long…? preguntamos por la duración. Respuestas cortas: Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.
text.de: Frage: Have / Has + Subjekt + been + Verb-ing. Mit How long…? fragen wir nach der Dauer. Kurzantworten: Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.

examples.es: How long have you been studying English?

tr.en: How long have you been studying English?
tr.de: Wie lange lernst du schon Englisch?

examples.es: Has she been working here long?

tr.en: Has she been working here long?

text.hu: Mostanáig tartó cselekvés, időtartammal: for, since, How long…?, all day, lately. A hangsúly a folyamaton és az időtartamon van.
text.en: An action that lasts up to now, with a duration: for, since, How long…?, all day, lately. The focus is on the process and how long it lasts.
text.es: Una acción que dura hasta ahora, con una duración: for, since, How long…?, all day, lately. El foco está en el proceso y cuánto dura.
text.de: Eine Handlung, die bis jetzt andauert, mit einer Dauer: for, since, How long…?, all day, lately. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Vorgang und seiner Dauer.

examples.es: She has been working here since May.

tr.en: She has been working here since May.

examples.es: It has been raining all day.

tr.en: It has been raining all day.
tr.es: Ha estado lloviendo todo el día.
tr.de: Es hat den ganzen Tag geregnet.

text.hu: Friss cselekvés, aminek most látszik az eredménye: valaki épp most hagyta abba, és a nyoma látszik (fáradt, vizes, piros szem).
text.en: A recent action whose result you can see now: someone has just stopped and there is a trace (tired, wet, red eyes).
text.es: Una acción reciente cuyo resultado se ve ahora: alguien acaba de parar y queda una huella (cansado, mojado, ojos rojos).
text.de: Eine frische Handlung, deren Ergebnis man jetzt sieht: Jemand hat gerade aufgehört und es bleibt eine Spur (müde, nass, rote Augen).

examples.es: You look tired. Have you been working?

tr.en: You look tired. Have you been working?
tr.de: Du siehst müde aus. Hast du gearbeitet?

examples.es: Her eyes are red. She has been crying.

tr.en: Her eyes are red. She has been crying.
tr.es: Tiene los ojos rojos. Ha estado llorando.
tr.de: Ihre Augen sind rot. Sie hat geweint.

text.hu: Folyamat vagy eredmény? Ha az időtartam a lényeg (How long?), folyamatos alak kell. Ha a darabszám vagy a kész eredmény (How many? three emails), egyszerű present perfect kell.
text.en: Process or result? When the duration matters (How long?), you need the continuous form. When the number or the finished result matters (How many? three emails), you need the simple present perfect.
text.es: ¿Proceso o resultado? Si importa la duración (How long?), hace falta la forma continua. Si importa el número o el resultado terminado (How many? three emails), hace falta el presente perfecto simple.
text.de: Vorgang oder Ergebnis? Wenn die Dauer wichtig ist (How long?), braucht man die Verlaufsform. Wenn die Anzahl oder das fertige Ergebnis wichtig ist (How many? three emails), braucht man das einfache Present Perfect.

examples.es: I have been writing emails all morning.

tr.en: I have been writing emails all morning.
tr.es: He estado escribiendo correos toda la mañana.
tr.de: Ich schreibe den ganzen Vormittag E-Mails.

text.hu: A „llevo dos horas esperando” angolul nem „I am waiting since two hours”. A mostanáig tartó idő mellé (for, since) present perfect continuous kell: „I have been waiting for two hours”.
text.en: “Llevo dos horas esperando” is not “I am waiting since two hours” in English. With time that lasts up to now (for, since) you need the present perfect continuous: “I have been waiting for two hours”.
text.es: «Llevo dos horas esperando» no es «I am waiting since two hours» en inglés. Con el tiempo que llega hasta ahora (for, since) hace falta el presente perfecto continuo: «I have been waiting for two hours».
text.de: „Llevo dos horas esperando“ heißt auf Englisch nicht „I am waiting since two hours“. Bei Zeit bis jetzt (for, since) braucht man das Present Perfect Continuous: „I have been waiting for two hours“.

text.hu: Az állapotot kifejező igéknek (know, like, love, want, have = birtokol, understand) szinte soha nincs folyamatos alakja. Nem „I have been knowing her”, hanem „I have known her for ten years”.
text.en: State verbs (know, like, love, want, have meaning own, understand) almost never have a continuous form. Not “I have been knowing her”, but “I have known her for ten years”.
text.es: Los verbos de estado (know, like, love, want, have con el sentido de tener, understand) casi nunca tienen forma continua. No «I have been knowing her», sino «I have known her for ten years».
text.de: Zustandsverben (know, like, love, want, have im Sinn von besitzen, understand) haben fast nie eine Verlaufsform. Nicht „I have been knowing her“, sondern „I have known her for ten years“.

text.hu: Darabszám vagy kész eredmény esetén egyszerű present perfect: „I have read two books this week”. Időtartam esetén folyamatos: „I have been reading all day”.
text.en: For a number or a finished result use the simple present perfect: “I have read two books this week”. For a duration use the continuous: “I have been reading all day”.
text.es: Para un número o un resultado terminado usa el presente perfecto simple: «I have read two books this week». Para una duración usa el continuo: «I have been reading all day».
text.de: Für eine Anzahl oder ein fertiges Ergebnis nimm das einfache Present Perfect: „I have read two books this week“. Für eine Dauer nimm die Verlaufsform: „I have been reading all day“.

text.hu: A been után mindig -ing alak áll: „I have been waiting”, nem „I have been wait” és nem „I have been waited”. Egyes szám harmadik személyben has kell: „he has been working”.
text.en: After been always comes the -ing form: “I have been waiting”, not “I have been wait” and not “I have been waited”. With he / she / it you need has: “he has been working”.
text.es: Después de been siempre va la forma -ing: «I have been waiting», no «I have been wait» ni «I have been waited». Con he / she / it hace falta has: «he has been working».
text.de: Nach been steht immer die -ing-Form: „I have been waiting“, nicht „I have been wait“ und nicht „I have been waited“. Bei he / she / it braucht man has: „he has been working“.

speak.hu: A folyamatos befejezett jelen szerkezete: «have» vagy «has», plusz «been», plusz az ige -ing alakja: «I have been waiting». Olyan cselekvésre használjuk, ami a múltban kezdődött és még tart: «I have been waiting for an hour», «she has been working here since May». Használjuk friss cselekvésre is, aminek látszik az eredménye: «You look tired. Have you been working?». Ha darabszám vagy kész eredmény a lényeg, egyszerű present perfect kell: «I have written three emails». Az állapotot kifejező igéknek nincs folyamatos alakjuk: nem «I have been knowing her», hanem «I have known her for years». Vigyázat: nem «I am waiting since two hours».
speak.en: The present perfect continuous is «have» or «has», plus «been», plus the -ing form of the verb: «I have been waiting». We use it for an action that started in the past and is still going on: «I have been waiting for an hour», «she has been working here since May». We also use it for a recent action whose result you can see: «You look tired. Have you been working?». When a number or a finished result matters, you need the simple present perfect: «I have written three emails». State verbs have no continuous form: not «I have been knowing her», but «I have known her for years». Careful: not «I am waiting since two hours».
speak.es: El presente perfecto continuo es «have» o «has», más «been», más la forma -ing del verbo: «I have been waiting». Se usa para una acción que empezó en el pasado y todavía continúa: «I have been waiting for an hour», «she has been working here since May». También se usa para una acción reciente cuyo resultado se ve: «You look tired. Have you been working?». Si importa un número o un resultado terminado, hace falta el presente perfecto simple: «I have written three emails». Los verbos de estado no tienen forma continua: no «I have been knowing her», sino «I have known her for years». Cuidado: no «I am waiting since two hours».
speak.de: Das Present Perfect Continuous besteht aus «have» oder «has», plus «been», plus der -ing-Form des Verbs: «I have been waiting». Man benutzt es für eine Handlung, die in der Vergangenheit begonnen hat und noch andauert: «I have been waiting for an hour», «she has been working here since May». Man benutzt es auch für eine frische Handlung, deren Ergebnis man sieht: «You look tired. Have you been working?». Wenn eine Anzahl oder ein fertiges Ergebnis wichtig ist, braucht man das einfache Present Perfect: «I have written three emails». Zustandsverben haben keine Verlaufsform: nicht «I have been knowing her», sondern «I have known her for years». Vorsicht: nicht «I am waiting since two hours».

items.sentence: I ___ for the bus for twenty minutes.

why.hu: A „for twenty minutes” a mostanáig tartó időt jelzi, ezért present perfect continuous kell: have been waiting.
why.en: “For twenty minutes” shows time that lasts up to now, so you need the present perfect continuous: have been waiting.
why.es: «For twenty minutes» indica tiempo que llega hasta ahora, así que hace falta el presente perfecto continuo: have been waiting.
why.de: „For twenty minutes“ zeigt Zeit bis jetzt, deshalb braucht man das Present Perfect Continuous: have been waiting.

am waiting.hu: Az „am waiting” csak a pillanatnyi cselekvést mondja; időtartammal (for twenty minutes) present perfect continuous kell.
am waiting.en: “Am waiting” only describes the action at this moment; with a duration (for twenty minutes) you need the present perfect continuous.
am waiting.es: «Am waiting» solo describe la acción en este momento; con una duración (for twenty minutes) hace falta el presente perfecto continuo.
am waiting.de: „Am waiting“ beschreibt nur die Handlung in diesem Moment; mit einer Dauer (for twenty minutes) braucht man das Present Perfect Continuous.

wait.hu: A „wait” egyszerű jelen, szokásra használjuk; a húsz perc óta tartó várakozáshoz have been waiting kell.
wait.en: “Wait” is the simple present, used for habits; waiting that has lasted twenty minutes needs have been waiting.
wait.es: «Wait» es el presente simple, que se usa para hábitos; una espera de veinte minutos necesita have been waiting.
wait.de: „Wait“ ist das Present Simple für Gewohnheiten; ein Warten, das zwanzig Minuten dauert, braucht have been waiting.

examples: She has been waiting for an hour.
We have been waiting here for a long time.

why.hu: A „since 2020” kezdőpont, és a tanulás még tart, ezért has been learning kell.
why.en: “Since 2020” is a starting point and the learning still goes on, so you need has been learning.
why.es: «Since 2020» es un punto de inicio y el aprendizaje continúa, así que hace falta has been learning.
why.de: „Since 2020“ ist ein Anfangspunkt und das Lernen geht weiter, deshalb braucht man has been learning.

is learning.hu: Az „is learning” nem fér össze a since-szel; a since mellé present perfect (continuous) áll.
is learning.en: “Is learning” does not go with since; since takes the present perfect (continuous).
is learning.es: «Is learning» no va con since; since lleva el presente perfecto (continuo).
is learning.de: „Is learning“ passt nicht zu since; since steht mit dem Present Perfect (Continuous).

learns.hu: A „learns” egyszerű jelen, de a since miatt a kezdet óta tartó időszakot present perfect fejezi ki.
learns.en: “Learns” is the simple present, but because of since the period from the start until now needs the present perfect.
learns.es: «Learns» es el presente simple, pero por since el periodo desde el inicio hasta ahora necesita el presente perfecto.
learns.de: „Learns“ ist das Present Simple, aber wegen since braucht der Zeitraum vom Anfang bis jetzt das Present Perfect.

examples: He has been working here since May.
They have been living here since last year.

items.sentence: How long has she ___ for this company?

why.hu: A has után been + ige-ing áll: has she been working.
why.en: After has comes been + verb-ing: has she been working.
why.es: Después de has va been + verbo-ing: has she been working.
why.de: Nach has steht been + Verb-ing: has she been working.

working.hu: A has mellett a „been” is kell: has she been working. A „has working” hiányos alak.
working.en: Besides has you also need “been”: has she been working. “Has working” is an incomplete form.
working.es: Además de has hace falta «been»: has she been working. «Has working» es una forma incompleta.
working.de: Neben has braucht man auch „been“: has she been working. „Has working“ ist eine unvollständige Form.

been work.hu: A been után -ing alak kell (working), nem az alapige.
been work.en: After been you need the -ing form (working), not the base verb.
been work.es: Después de been hace falta la forma -ing (working), no el verbo base.
been work.de: Nach been braucht man die -ing-Form (working), nicht die Grundform.

examples: How long has he been waiting?
How long have they been living here?

items.sentence: Your eyes are red. ___ you been crying?

why.hu: Friss cselekvés, aminek látszik az eredménye (piros szem): Have you been crying?
why.en: A recent action whose result you can see (red eyes): Have you been crying?
why.es: Una acción reciente cuyo resultado se ve (ojos rojos): Have you been crying?
why.de: Eine frische Handlung, deren Ergebnis man sieht (rote Augen): Have you been crying?

Are.hu: Az „Are you been” nem létező szerkezet; a been a have-vel együtt áll (Have you been crying?).
Are.en: “Are you been” is not a possible structure; been goes with have (Have you been crying?).
Are.es: «Are you been» no es una estructura posible; been va con have (Have you been crying?).
Are.de: „Are you been“ ist keine mögliche Struktur; been gehört zu have (Have you been crying?).

Did.hu: A did után alapige kell (Did you cry?), a „been crying” viszont have-vel alkot szerkezetet.
Did.en: After did you need the base verb (Did you cry?), but “been crying” forms a structure with have.
Did.es: Después de did hace falta el verbo base (Did you cry?), pero «been crying» forma la estructura con have.
Did.de: Nach did braucht man die Grundform (Did you cry?), „been crying“ bildet die Struktur aber mit have.

examples: Have you been walking?
Have you been sleeping?

items.sentence: The street is wet. It ___ all morning, but now it is sunny.

why.hu: Az „all morning” az eddig tartó időt jelzi, és az eredmény (vizes utca) látszik: has been raining.
why.en: “All morning” shows the time up to now, and the result (a wet street) is visible: has been raining.
why.es: «All morning» indica el tiempo hasta ahora y el resultado (una calle mojada) se ve: has been raining.
why.de: „All morning“ zeigt die Zeit bis jetzt, und das Ergebnis (eine nasse Straße) ist sichtbar: has been raining.

is raining.hu: Az „is raining” most zajló esőt jelent, de a mondat szerint most már napos az idő.
is raining.en: “Is raining” means rain at this moment, but the sentence says it is sunny now.
is raining.es: «Is raining» significa lluvia en este momento, pero la oración dice que ahora hace sol.
is raining.de: „Is raining“ heißt Regen in diesem Moment, aber der Satz sagt, dass es jetzt sonnig ist.

rains.hu: A „rains” egyszerű jelen, szokásra való; ez a mai délelőtti eső időtartamát nem fejezi ki.
rains.en: “Rains” is the simple present, used for habits; it does not express how long it rained this morning.
rains.es: «Rains» es el presente simple, para hábitos; no expresa cuánto tiempo llovió esta mañana.
rains.de: „Rains“ ist das Present Simple für Gewohnheiten; es drückt nicht aus, wie lange es heute Vormittag geregnet hat.

examples: It has been snowing all night.
The children have been playing outside.

why.hu: Darabszám (three emails) és kész eredmény: egyszerű present perfect, have written.
why.en: A number (three emails) and a finished result: the simple present perfect, have written.
why.es: Un número (three emails) y un resultado terminado: presente perfecto simple, have written.
why.de: Eine Anzahl (three emails) und ein fertiges Ergebnis: das einfache Present Perfect, have written.

have been writing.hu: A folyamatos alak a folyamatot és az időtartamot emeli ki; ha számot mondunk (three emails), egyszerű alak kell.
have been writing.en: The continuous form stresses the process and its duration; when you give a number (three emails), you need the simple form.
have been writing.es: La forma continua destaca el proceso y su duración; cuando das un número (three emails), hace falta la forma simple.
have been writing.de: Die Verlaufsform betont den Vorgang und seine Dauer; wenn man eine Anzahl nennt (three emails), braucht man die einfache Form.

am writing.hu: Az „am writing” a pillanatnyi cselekvés, de a mondat a délelőtt eddigi eredményét számolja össze.
am writing.en: “Am writing” is the action at this moment, but the sentence counts the result of the morning so far.
am writing.es: «Am writing» es la acción en este momento, pero la oración cuenta el resultado de la mañana hasta ahora.
am writing.de: „Am writing“ ist die Handlung in diesem Moment, aber der Satz zählt das bisherige Ergebnis des Vormittags.

examples: She has read two books this week.
We have made four calls today.

items.sentence: She is out of breath. She ___ in the park.

why.hu: Friss cselekvés, aminek látszik az eredménye (kifulladt): has been running.
why.en: A recent action whose result you can see (out of breath): has been running.
why.es: Una acción reciente cuyo resultado se ve (sin aliento): has been running.
why.de: Eine frische Handlung, deren Ergebnis man sieht (außer Atem): has been running.

runs.hu: A „runs” szokást fejez ki; itt egy friss, éppen befejezett cselekvés nyoma látszik, ezért has been running.
runs.en: “Runs” expresses a habit; here you see the trace of a recent action that just ended, so you need has been running.
runs.es: «Runs» expresa un hábito; aquí se ve la huella de una acción reciente que acaba de terminar, por eso has been running.
runs.de: „Runs“ drückt eine Gewohnheit aus; hier sieht man die Spur einer frischen, gerade beendeten Handlung, deshalb has been running.

is running.hu: Az „is running” azt mondaná, hogy most is fut; a mondat szerint viszont már itt van, és kifulladt.
is running.en: “Is running” would say she is running right now; the sentence says she is here, out of breath.
is running.es: «Is running» diría que está corriendo ahora mismo; la oración dice que ya está aquí, sin aliento.
is running.de: „Is running“ würde sagen, dass sie gerade läuft; der Satz sagt aber, dass sie schon hier ist und außer Atem.

examples: He has been walking for hours.
The kids have been playing all day.

why.hu: A „know” állapotot kifejező ige, nincs folyamatos alakja: I have known Maria for ten years.
why.en: “Know” is a state verb with no continuous form: I have known Maria for ten years.
why.es: «Know» es un verbo de estado sin forma continua: I have known Maria for ten years.
why.de: „Know“ ist ein Zustandsverb ohne Verlaufsform: I have known Maria for ten years.

have been knowing.hu: A know állapotot kifejező ige, ezért nem lehet -ing alakban használni: have known.
have been knowing.en: Know is a state verb, so it cannot be used in the -ing form: have known.
have been knowing.es: Know es un verbo de estado, por eso no se puede usar en la forma -ing: have known.
have been knowing.de: Know ist ein Zustandsverb und kann deshalb nicht in der -ing-Form stehen: have known.

am knowing.hu: Az „am knowing” nem helyes: a know nem folyamatos, és a for ten years present perfectet kér.
am knowing.en: “Am knowing” is wrong: know is never continuous, and for ten years asks for the present perfect.
am knowing.es: «Am knowing» es incorrecto: know nunca es continuo, y for ten years pide el presente perfecto.
am knowing.de: „Am knowing“ ist falsch: know steht nie in der Verlaufsform, und for ten years verlangt das Present Perfect.

examples: I have known him for years.
I have known Maria since school.

why.hu: A since 2018 a mostanáig tartó időszakot jelzi, ezért have been living kell.
why.en: “Since 2018” shows a period up to now, so you need have been living.
why.es: «Since 2018» indica un periodo hasta ahora, así que hace falta have been living.
why.de: „Since 2018“ zeigt einen Zeitraum bis jetzt, deshalb braucht man have been living.

live.hu: Spanyolul jelen idő áll („vivimos aquí desde 2018”), de angolul a since mellé present perfect kell.
live.en: Spanish uses the present (“vivimos aquí desde 2018”), but in English since needs the present perfect.
live.es: El español usa el presente («vivimos aquí desde 2018»), pero en inglés since necesita el presente perfecto.
live.de: Das Spanische benutzt das Präsens („vivimos aquí desde 2018“), aber im Englischen braucht since das Present Perfect.

are living.hu: Az „are living” sem megy a since-szel; a since mellé have been living (vagy have lived) áll.
are living.en: “Are living” does not go with since either; since takes have been living (or have lived).
are living.es: «Are living» tampoco va con since; since lleva have been living (o have lived).
are living.de: „Are living“ passt ebenfalls nicht zu since; since steht mit have been living (oder have lived).

examples: They have been living here since May.
I have been working here since June.

items.sentence: I ___ well lately, so I'm going to see a doctor.

why.hu: A „lately” a mostanáig tartó időszakra utal, az „I” mellé pedig haven’t kell: I haven’t been sleeping.
why.en: “Lately” points to a period up to now, and with “I” you need haven’t: I haven’t been sleeping.
why.es: «Lately» apunta a un periodo hasta ahora, y con «I» hace falta haven’t: I haven’t been sleeping.
why.de: „Lately“ verweist auf einen Zeitraum bis jetzt, und bei „I“ braucht man haven’t: I haven’t been sleeping.

am not sleeping.hu: Az „am not sleeping” csak a pillanatnyi állapotot írja le; a „lately” mostanáig tartó időszakot jelez.
am not sleeping.en: “Am not sleeping” only describes the moment; “lately” shows a period up to now.
am not sleeping.es: «Am not sleeping» solo describe el momento; «lately» indica un periodo hasta ahora.
am not sleeping.de: „Am not sleeping“ beschreibt nur den Moment; „lately“ zeigt einen Zeitraum bis jetzt.

hasn't been sleeping.hu: A hasn’t csak he / she / it mellé kerül; az „I” mellett haven’t áll.
hasn't been sleeping.en: Hasn’t only goes with he / she / it; with “I” you use haven’t.
hasn't been sleeping.es: Hasn’t solo va con he / she / it; con «I» se usa haven’t.
hasn't been sleeping.de: Hasn’t steht nur bei he / she / it; bei „I“ benutzt man haven’t.

examples: We have not been eating well.
They have not been working much.

items.sentence: ___ she been studying for the test?

why.hu: A she mellé has kell: Has she been studying…?
why.en: With she you need has: Has she been studying…?
why.es: Con she hace falta has: Has she been studying…?
why.de: Bei she braucht man has: Has she been studying…?

Is.hu: Az „Is she been” nem helyes; a been mindig a have / has után áll.
Is.en: “Is she been” is not correct; been always follows have / has.
Is.es: «Is she been» no es correcto; been siempre va después de have / has.
Is.de: „Is she been“ ist nicht korrekt; been steht immer nach have / has.

Did.hu: A did után alapige jön (Did she study?), a „been studying” viszont a has-szal alkot szerkezetet.
Did.en: After did comes the base verb (Did she study?), but “been studying” forms a structure with has.
Did.es: Después de did viene el verbo base (Did she study?), pero «been studying» forma la estructura con has.
Did.de: Nach did kommt die Grundform (Did she study?), „been studying“ bildet die Struktur aber mit has.

examples: Has he been sleeping?
Has she been waiting long?

items.sentence: My brother ___ been working here since May.

why.hu: A my brother = he, ezért has kell: has been working.
why.en: My brother = he, so you need has: has been working.
why.es: My brother = he, así que hace falta has: has been working.
why.de: My brother = he, deshalb braucht man has: has been working.

have.hu: A have az I, you, we, they mellé kerül; a my brother (he) mellé has kell.
have.en: Have goes with I, you, we, they; with my brother (he) you need has.
have.es: Have va con I, you, we, they; con my brother (he) hace falta has.
have.de: Have steht bei I, you, we, they; bei my brother (he) braucht man has.

is.hu: Az „is been working” nem létező alak; a been a have / has után áll.
is.en: “Is been working” is not a possible form; been follows have / has.
is.es: «Is been working» no es una forma posible; been va después de have / has.
is.de: „Is been working“ ist keine mögliche Form; been steht nach have / has.

examples: My mother has been working all day.
My friend has been waiting for an hour.

items.sentence: We have been ___ about this all day.

why.hu: A been után ige-ing áll: have been talking.
why.en: After been comes verb-ing: have been talking.
why.es: Después de been va verbo-ing: have been talking.
why.de: Nach been steht Verb-ing: have been talking.

talk.hu: A been után az -ing alak kell (talking), az alapige nem elég.
talk.en: After been you need the -ing form (talking), the base verb is not enough.
talk.es: Después de been hace falta la forma -ing (talking), el verbo base no basta.
talk.de: Nach been braucht man die -ing-Form (talking), die Grundform reicht nicht.

talked.hu: A talked múlt idő; a have been után az -ing alak áll, nem a múlt alak.
talked.en: “Talked” is a past form; after have been comes the -ing form, not the past form.
talked.es: «Talked» es una forma de pasado; después de have been va la forma -ing, no la de pasado.
talked.de: „Talked“ ist eine Vergangenheitsform; nach have been steht die -ing-Form, nicht die Vergangenheitsform.

examples: We have been working all day.
She has been reading all night.

items.sentence: She has been working here ___ last June.

why.hu: A „last June” kezdőpont, ezért since kell: since last June.
why.en: “Last June” is a starting point, so you need since: since last June.
why.es: «Last June» es un punto de inicio, así que hace falta since: since last June.
why.de: „Last June“ ist ein Anfangspunkt, deshalb braucht man since: since last June.

for.hu: A for időtartam elé kerül (for six months); a „last June” kezdőpont, nem időtartam.
for.en: For goes before a duration (for six months); “last June” is a starting point, not a duration.
for.es: For va antes de una duración (for six months); «last June» es un punto de inicio, no una duración.
for.de: For steht vor einer Dauer (for six months); „last June“ ist ein Anfangspunkt, keine Dauer.

ago.hu: Az „ago” egy időtartam után áll és egyszerű múlttal jár (six months ago); ide since kell.
ago.en: “Ago” follows a duration and goes with the past simple (six months ago); here you need since.
ago.es: «Ago» va después de una duración y con el pasado simple (six months ago); aquí hace falta since.
ago.de: „Ago“ steht nach einer Dauer und gehört zum Past Simple (six months ago); hier braucht man since.

examples: He has been here since Monday.
I have been sleeping since ten o’clock.

why.hu: A „lately” (mostanában) a mostanáig tartó időszakot jelzi, ezért illik a present perfect continuous mellé.
why.en: “Lately” means “in the recent past up to now”, so it fits the present perfect continuous.
why.es: «Lately» significa «últimamente», un periodo reciente hasta ahora, por eso encaja con el presente perfecto continuo.
why.de: „Lately“ bedeutet „in letzter Zeit“, einen Zeitraum bis jetzt, deshalb passt es zum Present Perfect Continuous.

yesterday.hu: A „yesterday” lezárt időpont, mellette egyszerű múlt kell (I felt tired yesterday).
yesterday.en: “Yesterday” is a finished time and needs the past simple (I felt tired yesterday).
yesterday.es: «Yesterday» es un momento terminado y pide el pasado simple (I felt tired yesterday).
yesterday.de: „Yesterday“ ist ein abgeschlossener Zeitpunkt und braucht das Past Simple (I felt tired yesterday).

tomorrow.hu: A „tomorrow” jövőre utal, a present perfect continuous viszont a mostanáig tartó időhöz kell.
tomorrow.en: “Tomorrow” points to the future, but the present perfect continuous needs time up to now.
tomorrow.es: «Tomorrow» apunta al futuro, pero el presente perfecto continuo necesita tiempo hasta ahora.
tomorrow.de: „Tomorrow“ verweist auf die Zukunft, das Present Perfect Continuous braucht aber Zeit bis jetzt.

examples: We have been working a lot lately.
She has been sleeping a lot lately.

items.sentence: I ___ the report at last. Here it is!

why.hu: A jelentés kész van (Here it is!), ezért egyszerű present perfect kell: have finished.
why.en: The report is done (Here it is!), so you need the simple present perfect: have finished.
why.es: El informe está terminado (Here it is!), así que hace falta el presente perfecto simple: have finished.
why.de: Der Bericht ist fertig (Here it is!), deshalb braucht man das einfache Present Perfect: have finished.

have been finishing.hu: A folyamatos alak a nem befejezett folyamatot emeli ki; itt a kész eredmény a lényeg, ezért have finished.
have been finishing.en: The continuous form stresses an unfinished process; here the finished result matters, so you need have finished.
have been finishing.es: La forma continua destaca un proceso no terminado; aquí importa el resultado terminado, por eso have finished.
have been finishing.de: Die Verlaufsform betont einen unfertigen Vorgang; hier ist das fertige Ergebnis wichtig, deshalb have finished.

am finishing.hu: Az „am finishing” még folyamatban lévő munkát jelent, de a jelentés már kész („Here it is!”).
am finishing.en: “Am finishing” means work still in progress, but the report is already done (“Here it is!”).
am finishing.es: «Am finishing» significa trabajo en curso, pero el informe ya está terminado («Here it is!»).
am finishing.de: „Am finishing“ heißt, dass die Arbeit noch läuft, aber der Bericht ist schon fertig („Here it is!“).

examples: I have finished my homework.
She has finished her work.

items.sentence: She ___ this car for five years.

why.hu: A „have” itt „birtokol”, állapotot kifejező ige, nincs folyamatos alakja: has had.
why.en: “Have” here means “own”, a state verb with no continuous form: has had.
why.es: «Have» aquí significa «tener» (poseer), un verbo de estado sin forma continua: has had.
why.de: „Have“ bedeutet hier „besitzen“, ein Zustandsverb ohne Verlaufsform: has had.

is having.hu: A „have” birtoklás jelentésben nem folyamatos; az „is having” itt helytelen.
is having.en: “Have” meaning ownership is not continuous; “is having” is wrong here.
is having.es: «Have» con el sentido de posesión no es continuo; «is having» es incorrecto aquí.
is having.de: „Have“ im Sinn von Besitz steht nicht in der Verlaufsform; „is having“ ist hier falsch.

has been having.hu: A birtoklást kifejező have nem kap -ing alakot, így a „has been having” nem helyes: has had.
has been having.en: The have that means ownership takes no -ing form, so “has been having” is not correct: has had.
has been having.es: El have que significa posesión no lleva forma -ing, por eso «has been having» no es correcto: has had.
has been having.de: Das have im Sinn von Besitz hat keine -ing-Form, deshalb ist „has been having“ nicht korrekt: has had.

examples: He has had this phone for years.
We have had a dog since May.
